issues.description: Endpoint path names are inconsistent: the problem statement and client controller expect REST endpoints under "/persons" (problem instructs POST/GET/PUT/DELETE /persons), and the client-side PersonController sends requests to "persons". However the server-side PersonResource in the solution exposes endpoints under "people" (e.g. @GetMapping("people"), @PostMapping("people")). This mismatch between client, problem description, and server implementation will prevent HTTP requests from reaching the server and confuses students which path they should implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the server endpoint paths consistent with the problem statement and client. Change the mappings in PersonResource from "people" to "persons" (e.g. @GetMapping("persons"), @PostMapping("persons"), @PutMapping("persons/{personId}"), @DeleteMapping("persons/{personId}")), or alternatively update the problem statement and client to use "people" consistently. Preferably align server to use "/persons" to match the exercise description and client controller.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies REST endpoints under /persons (e.g. POST /persons, GET /persons, PUT /persons/{personId}, DELETE /persons/{personId}), and the client implementation (PersonController) sends requests to the "persons" path. However, the server implementation in the solution uses the resource path "people" (e.g. @GetMapping("people"), @PostMapping("people") etc.). This divergent naming for the same conceptual resource (Person collection endpoints) creates a blocking mapping confusion for students: they cannot reliably map the problem requirements to the server implementation or to the client requests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the resource path name consistent across all artifacts. Prefer aligning the server to the problem statement and client by renaming the server endpoints from "people" to "persons" (update @GetMapping, @PostMapping, @PutMapping, @DeleteMapping to use "persons"). Alternatively, update the problem statement and client to use "people" — but ensure all three (problem, template/client, and server) use the same identifier.
